page: Microsoft Azure L4s_v4 is an x86_64 server instance from the Lsv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 4 vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for tile and int8 operations. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core, and includes 960 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not feature a GPU or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server demonstrates strong single-core performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2158.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 31.48 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are less competitive. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 3990.37 and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression of 26.74 GB/sec fall into the lower 25th percentile. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read and write speeds registering at 36.35 GB/sec and 25.49 GB/sec respectively. Large-model LLM inference is highly limited, with medium (7B) model text generation dropping to 4.52 tokens/sec, though small (135M) model prompt processing achieves 515.22 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the L4s_v4 offers a high ratio of local NVMe SSD storage and memory relative to its vCPU count, making it a dense resource option for storage-bound workloads without the premium cost of larger compute instances. It is well-suited for database operations, local caching, and web serving, as evidenced by its average Passmark database score of 2891.14 and static web serving throughput of 7.76 GB/sec. It is less suitable for highly parallel compute-intensive tasks, software compilation, or large-scale AI inference due to its multi-core and memory bandwidth limitations.
